pt.note: O capítulo final começa pela compreensão. Receptividade significa trabalhar as ideias com clareza para examiná-las, em vez de esperar que uma experiência extraordinária forneça seu significado.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Theosophy · GA 9 · Monges / Church, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: On the contrary, the more a man develops the capacity to refrain from allowing each feeling of sympathy and antipathy to be followed immediately by a judgment, an action, the finer will his sensitivity become.

en.quote: On the contrary, the more a man develops the capacity to refrain from allowing each feeling of sympathy and antipathy to be followed immediately by a judgment, an action, the finer will his sensitivity become.
en.note: The pause preserves the feeling while freeing judgment from automatic reaction. It is part of educating sensitivity as a means of knowledge.

pt.quote: Ao contrário, quanto mais alguém desenvolve a capacidade de impedir que cada sentimento de simpatia e antipatia seja seguido imediatamente por um julgamento ou uma ação, mais fina se torna sua sensibilidade.
pt.note: A pausa preserva o sentimento e liberta o julgamento da reação automática. Faz parte de educar a sensibilidade como meio de conhecimento.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Theosophy · GA 9 · Monges / Church, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: The seeker prepares himself for his task by overcoming through his own choice all the arbitrary thinking that naturally rules in him.

en.quote: The seeker prepares himself for his task by overcoming through his own choice all the arbitrary thinking that naturally rules in him.
en.note: The emphasis is on chosen coherence: one thought should connect intelligibly with the next. The example below makes that connection something you can perform and then examine.

pt.quote: O buscador se prepara para sua tarefa superando, por escolha própria, todo o pensar arbitrário que naturalmente o domina.
pt.note: A ênfase é na coerência escolhida: um pensamento deve ligar-se de modo inteligível ao seguinte. O exemplo permite realizar essa ligação e depois examiná-la.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Theosophy · GA 9 · Monges / Church, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: What is said here about the path of spiritual knowledge can all too easily, through failure to understand it, tempt us to consider it as a recommendation to cultivate certain moods of soul that would lead us to turn away from the immediate, joyous and strenuously active, experience of life.

en.quote: What is said here about the path of spiritual knowledge can all too easily, through failure to understand it, tempt us to consider it as a recommendation to cultivate certain moods of soul that would lead us to turn away from the immediate, joyous and strenuously active, experience of life.
en.note: The passage names a misunderstanding the conclusion corrects. The inner work is meant to deepen participation in life, so explain how a capacity studied in this chapter could change an ordinary action.

pt.quote: O que se diz aqui sobre o caminho do conhecimento espiritual pode, por incompreensão, levar a considerá-lo uma recomendação para cultivar disposições anímicas que nos afastariam da experiência imediata, alegre e intensamente ativa da vida.
pt.note: O trecho nomeia um equívoco que a conclusão corrige. O trabalho interior pretende aprofundar a participação na vida; explique como uma capacidade estudada pode transformar uma ação comum.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Theosophy · GA 9 · Monges / Church, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Just as in the body, eye and ear develop as organs of perception, as senses for bodily processes, so does a man develop in himself soul and spiritual organs of perception through which the soul and spiritual worlds are opened to him.

en.quote: Just as in the body, eye and ear develop as organs of perception, as senses for bodily processes, so does a man develop in himself soul and spiritual organs of perception through which the soul and spiritual worlds are opened to him.
en.note: Use this analogy to connect the four chapters: human constitution, biography and destiny, the worlds, and the development of knowing. Your synthesis should explain the links using passages, not merely list the terms.

pt.quote: Assim como olho e ouvido se desenvolvem no corpo como órgãos de percepção dos processos corporais, o ser humano desenvolve em si órgãos anímicos e espirituais de percepção pelos quais os mundos anímico e espiritual se abrem para ele.
pt.note: Use a analogia para relacionar os quatro capítulos: constituição humana, biografia e destino, os mundos e o desenvolvimento do conhecer. A síntese deve explicar as ligações por trechos, além de listar termos.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · John Salter
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: In order to grasp colour objectively we must try to keep within the world of colour itself and not leave it; then we may hope to penetrate its real nature.

en.quote: In order to grasp colour objectively we must try to keep within the world of colour itself and not leave it; then we may hope to penetrate its real nature.
en.note: This states the artistic method of the opening lectures: attend to colours and their relationships before reducing them to an external explanation. The course keeps observation and Steiner’s further interpretation distinguishable.

pt.quote: Para apreender a cor objetivamente, devemos procurar permanecer no próprio mundo da cor sem abandoná-lo; assim podemos esperar penetrar em sua verdadeira natureza.
pt.note: A frase apresenta o método artístico inicial: atender às cores e suas relações antes de reduzi-las a uma explicação externa. O curso distingue observação e interpretação adicional de Steiner.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · John Salter
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: From this circle we can see the relationships between certain fundamental colours: black, green, peach-blossom and white.

en.quote: From this circle we can see the relationships between certain fundamental colours: black, green, peach-blossom and white.
en.note: The circle organizes the four image colours through Steiner’s relations among lifelessness, life, soul and spirit. The lesson explains the four pairings and uses colour comparisons to make the relationships visible.

pt.quote: Nesse círculo podemos ver as relações entre certas cores fundamentais: preto, verde, flor de pessegueiro e branco.
pt.note: O círculo organiza as quatro cores-imagem pelas relações entre inanimado, vida, alma e espírito. A lição explica as correspondências e usa comparações de cores para tornar as relações visíveis.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · John Salter
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Yellow, blue and red have a lustre-character — something shines from them.

en.quote: Yellow, blue and red have a lustre-character — something shines from them.
en.note: Lustre names an active radiating quality, contrasted with an image of something. The lecture differentiates how yellow, blue and red want to spread; compare those directions in the studies below.

pt.quote: Amarelo, azul e vermelho possuem caráter de brilho: algo irradia deles.
pt.note: Brilho nomeia uma qualidade ativa de irradiação, contrastada com a imagem de algo. A palestra diferencia como amarelo, azul e vermelho tendem a se expandir; compare essas direções nos estudos abaixo.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · John Salter
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: And when he really lives in colour, the colour will itself be able to answer his question about the way in which it should be applied.

en.quote: And when he really lives in colour, the colour will itself be able to answer his question about the way in which it should be applied.
en.note: The subject is the painter. “Answer” describes a way of composing: the experienced quality of the colour guides its placement and the emerging form, instead of merely filling a prior outline.

pt.quote: E, quando ele realmente vive na cor, a própria cor poderá responder à sua pergunta sobre como deve ser aplicada.
pt.note: O sujeito é o pintor. “Responder” descreve uma maneira de compor: a qualidade vivenciada da cor orienta sua aplicação e a forma que surge, em vez de apenas preencher um contorno prévio.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · Pauline Wehrle
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Yet during Earth evolution man had to lose this state of living with his body within the flowing sea of colour, so that he might develop, in his ego, his own world outlook.

en.quote: Yet during Earth evolution man had to lose this state of living with his body within the flowing sea of colour, so that he might develop, in his ego, his own world outlook.
en.note: Steiner places artistic colour experience within a spiritual history of consciousness. The movement study illustrates a colour relationship; it does not by itself establish that history.

pt.quote: Contudo, durante a evolução terrestre, o ser humano precisou perder esse estado de viver corporalmente no mar fluente de cores para desenvolver, em seu eu, sua própria visão de mundo.
pt.note: Steiner situa a experiência artística da cor numa história espiritual da consciência. O estudo de movimento ilustra uma relação de cores; não estabelece, por si só, essa história.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · Pauline Wehrle
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: They will regard the tone as a kind of window through which they enter the spiritual world, and then it will not depend on a vague feeling of how one tone is added to another, to form melodies for instance, but by going through the tone the soul will also experience a moral-spiritual quality behind the separate tones.

en.quote: They will regard the tone as a kind of window through which they enter the spiritual world, and then it will not depend on a vague feeling of how one tone is added to another, to form melodies for instance, but by going through the tone the soul will also experience a moral-spiritual quality behind the separate tones.
en.note: The lecture describes art as a route toward the inner quality of experience. “Moral-spiritual” names the author’s intended depth, so do not reduce the colour-and-tone comparison to a pleasant mood alone.

pt.quote: Considerarão o som uma espécie de janela pela qual entram no mundo espiritual; isso não dependerá de uma sensação vaga de como um som se acrescenta a outro para formar melodias, pois, atravessando o som, a alma também vivenciará uma qualidade moral-espiritual por trás dos sons particulares.
pt.note: A palestra descreve a arte como caminho à qualidade interior da experiência. “Moral-espiritual” nomeia a profundidade pretendida; a comparação entre cor e som vai além de um estado de ânimo agradável.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · Pauline Wehrle
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: So you see there are these two world entities, light and darkness; light with its living thought and dying past, and darkness where the will germinates and the future comes into being.

en.quote: So you see there are these two world entities, light and darkness; light with its living thought and dying past, and darkness where the will germinates and the future comes into being.
en.note: The sentence gathers the lecture’s two correspondences: light–thought–past and darkness–will–future. Explain each relation within Steiner’s account before using light and dark as a compositional exercise.

pt.quote: Vemos assim essas duas entidades do mundo, luz e escuridão: a luz com seu pensamento vivo e passado que morre; a escuridão onde a vontade germina e o futuro vem a existir.
pt.note: A frase reúne duas correspondências: luz–pensamento–passado e escuridão–vontade–futuro. Explique cada relação na descrição de Steiner antes de usar claro e escuro num exercício de composição.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · Pauline Wehrle
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: If a person is honest with himself as regards the natural-scientific outlook of today, he will have to see things in the way I have just described, but this view can never build a bridge between the physical and the moral soul-element.

en.quote: If a person is honest with himself as regards the natural-scientific outlook of today, he will have to see things in the way I have just described, but this view can never build a bridge between the physical and the moral soul-element.
en.note: This states the problem the lecture tries to solve. A causal description of a bodily event and the meaning of a moral action answer different questions; Steiner seeks a spiritual account connecting them.

pt.quote: Se uma pessoa for honesta consigo quanto à visão científico-natural de hoje, terá de ver as coisas do modo que descrevi; mas essa visão nunca poderá construir uma ponte entre o físico e o elemento moral da alma.
pt.note: A frase enuncia o problema da palestra. Uma descrição causal do evento corporal e o significado da ação moral respondem a perguntas diferentes; Steiner busca uma descrição espiritual que os relacione.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · Pauline Wehrle
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: And the light seen through darkness, as you see at sunrise and sunset, looks red.

en.quote: And the light seen through darkness, as you see at sunrise and sunset, looks red.
en.note: Read this with the contrasting description of darkness seen through light. The lecture uses conditions of seeing to organize colour appearances; the study below asks you to describe the actual arrangement before explaining it.

pt.quote: E a luz vista através da escuridão, como no nascer e no pôr do sol, parece vermelha.
pt.note: Leia junto à descrição contrastante da escuridão vista através da luz. A palestra usa condições de visão para organizar aparências de cor; o estudo pede descrever a disposição real antes de explicá-la.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · Pauline Wehrle
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: For we need to acquire colour perspective again, the experience of what is near and far on a flat surface, not merely with the help of line perspective, which actually always makes use of a distorted sculptural element, but by means of colours receding and approaching through their inner quality and not through external lines.

en.quote: For we need to acquire colour perspective again, the experience of what is near and far on a flat surface, not merely with the help of line perspective, which actually always makes use of a distorted sculptural element, but by means of colours receding and approaching through their inner quality and not through external lines.
en.note: The central contrast is between two ways of creating depth. The exercise holds the surface flat and tests whether colour relationships alone change your experience of near and far.

pt.quote: Precisamos recuperar a perspectiva da cor: a experiência do próximo e do distante numa superfície plana, não apenas pela perspectiva linear, que usa um elemento escultórico deformado, mas por cores que recuam e avançam por sua qualidade interior, e não por linhas externas.
pt.note: O contraste central é entre duas maneiras de criar profundidade. O exercício mantém a superfície plana e examina se as relações de cor mudam a experiência de perto e longe.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · Pauline Wehrle
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: For the Apostles are down there in their brownish colouring, and Mary would not fit in.

en.quote: For the Apostles are down there in their brownish colouring, and Mary would not fit in.
en.note: Steiner is discussing Titian’s Assumption. The contrast between the earthly group and Mary’s ascent depends on colour relationships across the whole composition, not merely the depicted figures’ positions.

pt.quote: Pois os apóstolos estão ali embaixo com sua coloração acastanhada, e Maria não se ajustaria a ela.
pt.note: Steiner discute a Assunção de Ticiano. O contraste entre o grupo terrestre e a ascensão de Maria depende das relações de cor em toda a composição, além das posições das figuras.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · Pauline Wehrle
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: We must learn to paint out of the colour.

en.quote: We must learn to paint out of the colour.
en.note: This concise conclusion gives the portfolio its criterion: let relationships of colour generate form, depth and experienced weight. Show the initial and revised composition and explain the colour decision that changed it.

pt.quote: Devemos aprender a pintar a partir da cor.
pt.note: A conclusão oferece um critério ao portfólio: deixar que relações de cor gerem forma, profundidade e peso percebido. Mostre a composição inicial e a revista e explique a decisão cromática que a transformou.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Colour · 1992 translation · Pauline Wehrle
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: In the course of the hierarchies entering into evolution the Second Hierarchy appeared in the form of light and the Third Hierarchy in the form of colour.

en.quote: In the course of the hierarchies entering into evolution the Second Hierarchy appeared in the form of light and the Third Hierarchy in the form of colour.
en.note: The rainbow is interpreted within a cosmology of spiritual beings. Reconstruct that order and its relation to warmth, light and colour; it is a different task from observing the physical appearance of a rainbow.

pt.quote: No decorrer da entrada das hierarquias na evolução, a Segunda Hierarquia apareceu na forma de luz e a Terceira, na forma de cor.
pt.note: O arco-íris é interpretado numa cosmologia de seres espirituais. Reconstrua essa ordem e sua relação com calor, luz e cor; é uma tarefa distinta de observar a aparência física do arco-íris.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: A particular age in life, such as the ninth year, can best be studied if we survey the larger period in which it occurs.

en.quote: A particular age in life, such as the ninth year, can best be studied if we survey the larger period in which it occurs.
en.note: This is the book’s developmental method: interpret a transition in relation to what comes before and after. Koepke places the ninth year within the second seven-year period; the course examines that model through particular encounters.

pt.quote: Uma idade particular da vida, como o nono ano, pode ser melhor estudada quando examinamos o período mais amplo em que ocorre.
pt.note: Este é o método de desenvolvimento do livro: interpretar uma transição em relação ao que a precede e sucede. Koepke situa o nono ano no segundo setênio; o curso examina esse modelo por encontros particulares.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: When it was almost finished, the children begged the teacher to make a door for it, otherwise one would not be able to shut out the world and be alone in the house.

en.quote: When it was almost finished, the children begged the teacher to make a door for it, otherwise one would not be able to shut out the world and be alone in the house.
en.note: The little wooden house makes a theme in the Peter conversation concrete: the child seeks an inner space with a boundary. The adult’s practical response becomes part of the encounter, rather than only an interpretation of the child.

pt.quote: Quando estava quase pronta, as crianças pediram ao professor que fizesse uma porta; caso contrário, não seria possível fechar o mundo do lado de fora e ficar sozinho na casa.
pt.note: A pequena casa de madeira concretiza um tema da conversa sobre Peter: a criança busca um espaço interior com limite. A resposta prática do adulto passa a integrar o encontro, além da interpretação da criança.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Nor is it so often seen what decisive turns in life are being prepared for in the depths of the child's soul.

en.quote: Nor is it so often seen what decisive turns in life are being prepared for in the depths of the child's soul.
en.note: This sentence belongs to the constructed discussion of Monica. Koepke asks the adults to take inward change seriously; the conversation also leaves room for more than one interpretation of her fear.

pt.quote: Tampouco se percebe com frequência que mudanças decisivas da vida estão sendo preparadas nas profundezas da alma da criança.
pt.note: A frase pertence à conversa construída sobre Monica. Koepke pede que os adultos levem a mudança interior a sério; a conversa também deixa espaço para mais de uma interpretação do medo.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Of course, the parents must also speak with the child about replacing the money. The child himself can use his imagination and make suggestions for what he should do.

en.quote: Of course, the parents must also speak with the child about replacing the money. The child himself can use his imagination and make suggestions for what he should do.
en.note: The passage follows a conversation about taking money. Repair is part of the teaching, and the child participates in imagining it. Use this relation between understanding, responsibility and participation in your final case study.

pt.quote: É claro que os pais também precisam conversar com a criança sobre devolver o dinheiro. A própria criança pode usar a imaginação e sugerir o que deve fazer.
pt.note: O trecho vem após uma conversa sobre pegar dinheiro. Reparar integra a aprendizagem, e a criança participa imaginando a reparação. Use essa relação entre compreensão, responsabilidade e participação no estudo final.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: But the content of the picture—death—remained a motif in Kokoschka's life and took precedence again and again in his work.

en.quote: But the content of the picture—death—remained a motif in Kokoschka's life and took precedence again and again in his work.
en.note: Koepke reads a remembered encounter in the light of later artistic work. The link is biographical interpretation: a recurring motif makes a childhood experience meaningful without proving that it determined the whole life.

pt.quote: Mas o conteúdo da imagem — a morte — permaneceu um motivo na vida de Kokoschka e voltou a ocupar lugar de destaque em sua obra.
pt.note: Koepke lê um encontro lembrado à luz da obra artística posterior. A ligação é interpretação biográfica: um motivo recorrente torna a experiência significativa sem provar que determinou toda a vida.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Sixth Grader: The spirit in the head, now fully awake, penetrates into the sensory world and discovers the imaginative realm in the sleeping depths of its own soul.

en.quote: Sixth Grader: The spirit in the head, now fully awake, penetrates into the sensory world and discovers the imaginative realm in the sleeping depths of its own soul.
en.note: Read this alongside the preceding first-grade description. Koepke proposes a reversal in the relation between imagination and sensory understanding, then compares the head, limbs and rhythmic middle.

pt.quote: Aluno do sexto ano: o espírito na cabeça, agora plenamente desperto, penetra no mundo sensorial e descobre o reino imaginativo nas profundezas adormecidas da própria alma.
pt.note: Leia junto à descrição anterior do primeiro ano. Koepke propõe uma inversão na relação entre imaginação e compreensão sensorial e compara cabeça, membros e região rítmica intermediária.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: One could say that the children have “moved within their own house,” have taken more completely possession of their own house.

en.quote: One could say that the children have “moved within their own house,” have taken more completely possession of their own house.
en.note: The house is an image for the child’s own organization. The chapter connects a stronger inward standpoint with changed relations to perception, feeling and the surrounding world.

pt.quote: Pode-se dizer que as crianças “se mudaram dentro da própria casa”, tomando posse dela de modo mais completo.
pt.note: A casa é imagem da própria organização da criança. O capítulo relaciona um ponto de vista interior mais forte a mudanças na percepção, no sentir e no vínculo com o mundo.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: In this activity children experience the forming of their own inner space, and this experience of space is just what the children are seeking.

en.quote: In this activity children experience the forming of their own inner space, and this experience of space is just what the children are seeking.
en.note: The context is the curriculum’s work with shelter and building. Koepke connects useful material activity with the transition’s inward theme, so the educational task should explain both the work and its proposed significance.

pt.quote: Nessa atividade, as crianças vivenciam a formação de seu próprio espaço interior; é justamente essa experiência do espaço que procuram.
pt.note: O contexto é o trabalho curricular com abrigo e construção. Koepke relaciona atividade material útil e tema interior da transição; a tarefa educativa deve explicar o trabalho e o significado proposto.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: It is the pressure to perform that constricts the breathing like the bodice laced too tightly, the report-card pressures that, like the poisoned comb in the hair, give rise to nervous troubles.

en.quote: It is the pressure to perform that constricts the breathing like the bodice laced too tightly, the report-card pressures that, like the poisoned comb in the hair, give rise to nervous troubles.
en.note: This is Koepke’s use of Snow White imagery to interpret performance pressure. Distinguish the story image, the educational concern and the bodily claims; an analogy can open a question without establishing a diagnosis.

pt.quote: É a pressão por desempenho que aperta a respiração como o corpete excessivamente amarrado; as pressões do boletim, como o pente envenenado nos cabelos, provocam perturbações nervosas.
pt.note: Koepke usa imagens de Branca de Neve para interpretar a pressão por desempenho. Distinga imagem narrativa, preocupação educativa e afirmações corporais; a analogia abre uma pergunta sem estabelecer um diagnóstico.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Thus, there are three motifs that children in this age can take in: the divine origin of human beings, the lighting-up of life in death, and the realm of art.

en.quote: Thus, there are three motifs that children in this age can take in: the divine origin of human beings, the lighting-up of life in death, and the realm of art.
en.note: The next sentence connects these motifs with Father, Son and Holy Spirit. The chapter’s proposal is explicitly Christian and anthroposophical; explain its symbolic structure before considering an educational application.

pt.quote: Há, assim, três motivos que crianças dessa idade podem acolher: a origem divina do ser humano, a iluminação da vida na morte e o reino da arte.
pt.note: A frase seguinte relaciona os motivos ao Pai, ao Filho e ao Espírito Santo. A proposta é explicitamente cristã e antroposófica; explique sua estrutura simbólica antes de considerar uma aplicação educativa.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Under the guidance of iron the I works its way with certainty through the critical phase of the ninth year.

en.quote: Under the guidance of iron the I works its way with certainty through the critical phase of the ninth year.
en.note: This sentence belongs to the historical school-doctor discussion. It connects a material substance with incarnation of the I. Study that explanatory claim and its assumptions here; it is not a treatment instruction.

pt.quote: Sob a orientação do ferro, o Eu abre seu caminho com segurança pela fase crítica do nono ano.
pt.note: A frase pertence à discussão histórica do médico escolar. Relaciona uma substância material à encarnação do Eu. Estude a afirmação e seus pressupostos; ela não é uma instrução de tratamento.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: The wind carried this little seed high up into the sky; it flew over a deep chasm.

en.quote: The wind carried this little seed high up into the sky; it flew over a deep chasm.
en.note: The story begins with displacement and follows the seed toward rooted belonging. Explain how that movement speaks to the book’s transition theme while leaving room for the child’s own response to the story.

pt.quote: O vento levou a pequena semente bem alto no céu; ela voou sobre um abismo profundo.
pt.note: A história começa com deslocamento e acompanha a semente até o enraizamento. Explique como esse movimento se relaciona à transição, deixando espaço para a resposta da criança à narrativa.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Just as in the development of the child between the seventh and the twelfth year we see a reversal that begins in the ninth year, so after a period of nine and one-third years, so the moon reverses the relationship of its own orbit to that of the sun, the ecliptic.

en.quote: Just as in the development of the child between the seventh and the twelfth year we see a reversal that begins in the ninth year, so after a period of nine and one-third years, so the moon reverses the relationship of its own orbit to that of the sun, the ecliptic.
en.note: The appendix proposes a correspondence between two rhythms. Identify the two patterns separately before assessing the suggested connection; a numerical resemblance does not alone establish a developmental cause.

pt.quote: Assim como no desenvolvimento da criança entre sete e doze anos vemos uma inversão que começa no nono ano, após nove anos e um terço a Lua inverte a relação de sua órbita com a órbita aparente do Sol, a eclíptica.
pt.note: O apêndice propõe uma correspondência entre dois ritmos. Identifique os padrões separadamente antes de avaliar sua ligação; semelhança numérica não estabelece sozinha uma causa do desenvolvimento.

author: Hermann Koepke
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: If we observe the change of teeth in children, we can see that the principle of reversal as it operates in the ninth year is also at work in the process of teeth formation.

en.quote: If we observe the change of teeth in children, we can see that the principle of reversal as it operates in the ninth year is also at work in the process of teeth formation.
en.note: This introduces the appendix’s organizing analogy. Read the tooth sequence and the proposed reversal as separate steps in an argument; ask what observation would support the connection being made.

pt.quote: Se observarmos a troca dos dentes nas crianças, podemos ver que o princípio de inversão, tal como atua no nono ano, também atua no processo de formação dos dentes.
pt.note: Isso introduz a analogia organizadora do apêndice. Leia a sequência dentária e a inversão proposta como passos distintos de uma argumentação; pergunte que observação sustentaria a ligação.

author: Rudolf Steiner, quoted in Koepke’s form-drawing appendix
title: Encountering the Self · Jesse Darrell translation, 1989
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Have them imagine what is needed to finish it. You try in every way possible to get the children to finish the drawing.

en.quote: Have them imagine what is needed to finish it. You try in every way possible to get the children to finish the drawing.
en.note: Steiner’s quoted instruction follows an unfinished form on the board. The activity cultivates inward completion and a relation between parts and whole; the task below makes that relation visible in your drawing.

pt.quote: Peça que imaginem o que é necessário para completá-lo. Procure, de todas as maneiras possíveis, levar as crianças a concluir o desenho.
pt.note: A instrução citada de Steiner segue uma forma inacabada no quadro. A atividade cultiva a complementação interior e a relação entre partes e todo; a tarefa torna essa relação visível no desenho.

author: Editorial introduction to the 1971 edition
title: Ancient Myths · M. Cotterell translation, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: The following lectures were given by Rudolf Steiner to an audience familiar with the general background and terminology of his anthroposophical teaching.

en.quote: The following lectures were given by Rudolf Steiner to an audience familiar with the general background and terminology of his anthroposophical teaching.
en.note: The edition warns that these are lectures with assumed background knowledge. Begin by separating the myth’s narrative, Steiner’s interpretation and the concepts his interpretation presupposes.

pt.quote: As palestras seguintes foram dadas por Rudolf Steiner a um público familiarizado com o contexto geral e a terminologia de seu ensinamento antroposófico.
pt.note: A edição esclarece que as palestras pressupõem conhecimentos anteriores. Comece distinguindo a narrativa do mito, a interpretação de Steiner e os conceitos que ela pressupõe.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Ancient Myths · M. Cotterell translation, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: We observe from the whole way in which Greek and Egyptian stood to their Gods, that at the same time there was expressed in this consciousness a remembrance of the ancient times of atavistic clairvoyance.

en.quote: We observe from the whole way in which Greek and Egyptian stood to their Gods, that at the same time there was expressed in this consciousness a remembrance of the ancient times of atavistic clairvoyance.
en.note: Steiner reads the myths as memories of changed consciousness. First follow the stories of Osiris and the Greek divine generations, then identify how he connects each narrative structure with that claim.

pt.quote: Observamos, em toda a maneira como gregos e egípcios se relacionavam com seus deuses, que essa consciência expressava uma lembrança dos tempos antigos de clarividência atávica.
pt.note: Steiner lê os mitos como lembranças de uma consciência transformada. Acompanhe primeiro Osíris e as gerações divinas gregas; depois identifique como relaciona suas estruturas narrativas à afirmação.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Ancient Myths · M. Cotterell translation, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Mankind is again to achieve vision directed to the supersensible; it is to be achieved on the path of Spiritual Science, through spiritual scientific thinking.

en.quote: Mankind is again to achieve vision directed to the supersensible; it is to be achieved on the path of Spiritual Science, through spiritual scientific thinking.
en.note: The lecture’s direction is a renewed form of knowing, not simply a return to ancient imagery. Its discussion of language and abstraction asks what was lost and how it might be transformed.

pt.quote: A humanidade deve voltar a alcançar uma visão dirigida ao suprassensível; isso deve ocorrer pelo caminho da ciência espiritual, por meio do pensar científico-espiritual.
pt.note: A direção é uma forma renovada de conhecer, além de retornar às imagens antigas. A discussão de linguagem e abstração pergunta o que se perdeu e como isso pode ser transformado.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Ancient Myths · M. Cotterell translation, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: We have indicated how the ancient Osiris-Isis myth was in fact connected with the vanishing of the alteration of the soul.

en.quote: We have indicated how the ancient Osiris-Isis myth was in fact connected with the vanishing of the alteration of the soul.
en.note: The surrounding argument links bodily maturity, inward development and changing access to spiritual experience. The veil of Isis gives that question a mythic form; explain the form before interpreting its modern transformation.

pt.quote: Indicamos como o antigo mito de Osíris e Ísis se relacionava ao desaparecimento da transformação da alma.
pt.note: A argumentação relaciona maturidade corporal, desenvolvimento interior e mudança de acesso à experiência espiritual. O véu de Ísis dá forma mítica à pergunta; explique-a antes de interpretar sua transformação moderna.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Ancient Myths · M. Cotterell translation, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: What impulses of human life must enter especially into the consciousness of man today so that a counterweight may be created to the principle of heredity that prevails almost exclusively — whether in science or in general life?

en.quote: What impulses of human life must enter especially into the consciousness of man today so that a counterweight may be created to the principle of heredity that prevails almost exclusively — whether in science or in general life?
en.note: This is the lecture’s explicit problem. Steiner seeks room for spiritual individuality beyond inherited determination; connect his answer with the earlier mythic account and keep it distinct from a biological demonstration.

pt.quote: Que impulsos da vida humana precisam entrar especialmente na consciência atual para criar um contrapeso ao princípio da hereditariedade, que predomina quase exclusivamente na ciência ou na vida em geral?
pt.note: Este é o problema explícito da palestra. Steiner busca espaço para a individualidade espiritual além da determinação herdada; relacione sua resposta ao relato mítico anterior e distinga-a de uma demonstração biológica.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Ancient Myths · M. Cotterell translation, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: If today we wish to have a development of the soul and spirit nature after our twenties, we must seek for this development by our power of will.

en.quote: If today we wish to have a development of the soul and spirit nature after our twenties, we must seek for this development by our power of will.
en.note: The lecture contrasts development supplied by nature with development deliberately taken up. It places this contrast within a historical account of humanity’s ages; the course’s lifelong-learning activity explores the deliberate element.

pt.quote: Se hoje desejamos desenvolver a natureza anímica e espiritual depois dos vinte e poucos anos, precisamos buscar esse desenvolvimento pela força de nossa vontade.
pt.note: A palestra distingue desenvolvimento fornecido pela natureza e desenvolvimento assumido deliberadamente. Situa o contraste numa descrição histórica das idades da humanidade; a atividade de aprendizagem contínua explora o elemento deliberado.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Ancient Myths · M. Cotterell translation, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Because men do not keep the inner livingness their heart grows cold; the heart warmth does not stream up to the head; love, which comes from the rest of the organism, does not fructify the head.

en.quote: Because men do not keep the inner livingness their heart grows cold; the heart warmth does not stream up to the head; love, which comes from the rest of the organism, does not fructify the head.
en.note: “Heart-knowledge” concerns ideas becoming part of the whole person over time. Steiner gives this a spiritual and bodily account; the example asks what changes when an understood idea enters an actual encounter.

pt.quote: Como as pessoas não conservam a vitalidade interior, seu coração esfria; o calor do coração não sobe à cabeça; o amor, que vem do restante do organismo, não fecunda a cabeça.
pt.note: O “conhecimento do coração” diz respeito a ideias que integram a pessoa inteira ao longo do tempo. Steiner apresenta uma descrição espiritual e corporal; o exemplo pergunta o que muda quando uma ideia compreendida entra num encontro real.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Ancient Myths · M. Cotterell translation, 1971
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: This education must be given through all sorts of narratives, all sorts of things which are adapted moreover to youth — but so adapted that one can keep one's interest in them through every age of life.

en.quote: This education must be given through all sorts of narratives, all sorts of things which are adapted moreover to youth — but so adapted that one can keep one's interest in them through every age of life.
en.note: This gives the final project its test: a story should sustain renewed understanding, not only deliver a quick moral. Explain its anthroposophical idea, adapt it to your audience and revise it in light of their response.

pt.quote: Essa educação deve ser oferecida por diferentes narrativas e materiais adaptados à juventude, mas de tal modo que possam conservar o interesse em todas as idades da vida.
pt.note: A frase oferece um critério ao projeto final: uma história deve sustentar compreensão renovada, além de transmitir uma moral rápida. Explique a ideia antroposófica, adapte-a ao público e revise-a conforme a resposta recebida.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Four Temperaments · GA 57 · 4 March 1909
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Dieses einzelne Rätsel ist nicht durch das Hinpfahlen der abstrakten Vorstellungen und Begriffe zu lösen, sondern wir müssen jedem einzelnen Menschen so entgegentreten, daß wir ihm unmittelbares Verständnis entgegenbringen.

en.quote: This individual riddle cannot be solved by planting abstract representations and concepts in front of it; we must approach each individual human being with direct understanding.
en.note: The lecture ends by returning from general types to the individual encounter. Use the framework to improve your attention to someone, and check whether your final account contains more understanding than the first label did.

pt.quote: Esse enigma individual não se resolve colocando diante dele representações e conceitos abstratos; precisamos nos aproximar de cada ser humano com compreensão direta.
pt.note: A palestra termina retornando dos tipos gerais ao encontro individual. Use o quadro para melhorar a atenção à pessoa e confira se o relato final contém mais compreensão que o primeiro rótulo.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Four Temperaments · GA 57 · 4 March 1909
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Dadurch nun, daß zwei Strömungen im Menschen zusammenfließen, wenn er hineintritt in die physische Welt, dadurch entsteht eine verschiedene Mischung der vier Wesensglieder des Menschen, und eines erhält sozusagen die Herrschaft über die anderen und drückt ihnen die Färbung auf.

en.quote: As two streams converge in the human being on entering the physical world, different mixtures of the four members arise; one, so to speak, takes the lead and gives the others its colouring.
en.note: The two streams are individuality and heredity. Temperament names their meeting in a particular balance of the four members; predominance does not mean that the other members are absent.

pt.quote: Quando duas correntes convergem no ser humano ao entrar no mundo físico, surgem diferentes combinações dos quatro membros; um deles, por assim dizer, assume a direção e dá sua coloração aos outros.
pt.note: As duas correntes são individualidade e hereditariedade. Temperamento nomeia seu encontro num equilíbrio particular dos quatro membros; predominância não significa ausência dos demais.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Four Temperaments · GA 57 · 4 March 1909
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Dadurch tritt er auf als der Mensch, der sein Ich unter allen Umständen durchsetzen will.

en.quote: He therefore appears as the person who wants to assert his I under all circumstances.
en.note: The preceding sentence associates the choleric temperament with predominance of the I. The portrait concerns directed will meeting resistance; the educational question is how purpose can develop along with receptivity to correction.

pt.quote: Ele aparece, assim, como a pessoa que quer afirmar seu Eu em todas as circunstâncias.
pt.note: A frase anterior associa o temperamento colérico à predominância do Eu. O retrato trata da vontade dirigida que encontra resistência; a pergunta educativa é como desenvolver propósito e abertura à correção.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Four Temperaments · GA 57 · 4 March 1909
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Er eilt von Lebenseindruck zu Lebenseindruck, von Wahrnehmung zu Wahrnehmung.

en.quote: He hurries from one impression of life to another, from perception to perception.
en.note: This describes the movement of sanguine interest. Steiner connects it with the astral member; the practical task is to find a meaningful thread that can invite return without suppressing responsiveness.

pt.quote: Ele passa rapidamente de uma impressão da vida a outra, de uma percepção a outra.
pt.note: A frase descreve o movimento do interesse sanguíneo. Steiner o relaciona ao membro astral; a tarefa prática é encontrar um fio significativo que convide ao retorno sem suprimir a receptividade.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Four Temperaments · GA 57 · 4 March 1909
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Wir sahen, daß das phlegmatische Temperament dadurch entsteht, daß vorherrschend gemacht ist das, was wir Äther- oder Lebensleib nennen, das, was des Menschen Wachstums- und Lebensvorgänge im Innern regelt.

en.quote: We saw that the phlegmatic temperament arises when what we call the etheric or life body predominates, regulating the human being’s inner processes of growth and life.
en.note: The lecture connects this predominance with inward ease and steadiness. The course then asks what kind of invitation connects that steadiness with participation in a shared activity.

pt.quote: Vimos que o temperamento fleumático surge quando predomina o que chamamos corpo etérico ou vital, que regula interiormente os processos humanos de crescimento e vida.
pt.note: A palestra relaciona essa predominância ao bem-estar interior e à constância. O curso pergunta que convite relaciona essa constância à participação numa atividade compartilhada.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Four Temperaments · GA 57 · 4 March 1909
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Denn der physische Leib ist das Instrument, das er durch seine höheren Glieder überall beherrschen soll; jetzt aber herrscht dieser physische Leib, setzt dem anderen Widerstand entgegen.

en.quote: For the physical body is the instrument to be directed through the higher members; here, however, the physical body predominates and offers resistance to the others.
en.note: Resistance is the key to Steiner’s melancholic portrait. His explanation links it with pain and inward sensitivity; the application should seek understanding and care for a person rather than assume the cause of their suffering.

pt.quote: O corpo físico é o instrumento a ser dirigido pelos membros superiores; aqui, porém, ele predomina e oferece resistência aos demais.
pt.note: A resistência é a chave do retrato melancólico. Steiner a relaciona à dor e à sensibilidade interior; a aplicação deve buscar compreensão e cuidado, sem presumir a causa do sofrimento.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Four Temperaments · GA 57 · 4 March 1909
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Ich habe Ihnen hier die Grundtypen angeführt. So rein kommen sie im Leben natürlich nicht vor. Jeder Mensch hat nur den Grundton eines Temperamentes, daneben hat er von den anderen.

en.quote: I have presented the basic types here. Naturally, they do not occur in life in such a pure form. Each person has the fundamental tone of one temperament, alongside elements of the others.
en.note: This qualification belongs to the original lecture. A portrait simplifies a pattern; encountering a mixed and changing person requires returning from the pattern to what actually happens.

pt.quote: Apresentei aqui os tipos básicos. Naturalmente, eles não aparecem na vida de forma tão pura. Cada pessoa possui o tom fundamental de um temperamento, ao lado de elementos dos outros.
pt.note: A ressalva pertence à palestra original. Um retrato simplifica um padrão; encontrar uma pessoa com tendências combinadas exige retornar do padrão ao que realmente acontece.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Four Temperaments · GA 57 · 4 March 1909
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Aber um die Temperamente zu leiten, ist der Grundsatz zu beachten, daß immer mit dem gerechnet werden muß, was da ist, nicht mit dem, was nicht da ist.

en.quote: To guide the temperaments, observe the principle of always working with what is present, not with what is absent.
en.note: The following examples start from an existing interest or relationship. The educational task is to find a workable point of contact, then shape an activity through which a capacity can grow.

pt.quote: Para orientar os temperamentos, observe o princípio de trabalhar sempre com o que está presente, e não com o que está ausente.
pt.note: Os exemplos seguintes partem de um interesse ou vínculo existente. A tarefa educativa é encontrar um ponto de contato e formar uma atividade pela qual uma capacidade possa crescer.

author: Gilbert Childs
title: Understand Your Temperament! · Chapter 7
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: we are all dependent on one another

en.quote: we are all dependent on one another
en.note: This phrase is part of Childs’s discussion of rank and cooperation at work. It gives the practical chapter a relational starting point: a role must serve the shared task, and should be reviewed through actual skills and contributions.

pt.quote: todos dependemos uns dos outros
pt.note: A expressão integra a discussão de Childs sobre hierarquia e cooperação no trabalho. Oferece um ponto de partida relacional: o papel deve servir à tarefa compartilhada e ser revisto pelas capacidades e contribuições reais.

author: Gilbert Childs
title: Understand Your Temperament! · Chapter 8
edition: Selected excerpt from the supplied English edition; Brazilian Portuguese is a new course translation. Line breaks normalized.
original: Various aspects of reality are of course present, but in the main the sketches of both temperamental attributes, and obviously the situations, are deliberately skewed.

en.quote: Various aspects of reality are of course present, but in the main the sketches of both temperamental attributes, and obviously the situations, are deliberately skewed.
en.note: Childs qualifies his compatibility sketches as exaggerated portraits. Use them to formulate questions about pace, privacy and decision-making; the actual relationship must supply the answers.

pt.quote: Aspectos da realidade estão presentes, é claro, mas, em geral, os esboços das características temperamentais e das situações são deliberadamente distorcidos.
pt.note: Childs ressalva que os esboços de compatibilidade são retratos exagerados. Use-os para formular perguntas sobre ritmo, privacidade e decisões; a relação real deve fornecer as respostas.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Four Temperaments · GA 57 · 4 March 1909
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Wir können uns durch den Verstand Erlebnisse schaffen, für die das kurze Interesse des Sanguinikers berechtigt ist.

en.quote: Through our understanding, we can arrange experiences for which the sanguine person’s brief interest is appropriate.
en.note: This illustrates indirect self-education: change the circumstances in which a tendency works instead of merely ordering yourself to stop having it. The small experiment below must name both the tendency and the deliberately arranged condition.

pt.quote: Por nossa compreensão, podemos organizar experiências nas quais o interesse breve do sanguíneo seja apropriado.
pt.note: Isso ilustra autoeducação indireta: mudar as circunstâncias em que atua uma tendência, em vez de apenas ordenar que ela desapareça. O pequeno experimento deve nomear a tendência e a condição organizada deliberadamente.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Parallel reading · How to Know Higher Worlds · Meditation
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Diese Meditation ist das Mittel zu übersinnlicher Erkenntnis.

en.quote: This meditation is the means to supersensible knowledge.
en.note: This parallel passage from GA 10 states Steiner’s intended horizon. The preceding sentence describes a soul-life in thought expanding toward spiritual being. Study the meaning of a selected text before working meditatively with it.

pt.quote: Essa meditação é o meio para o conhecimento suprassensível.
pt.note: Este trecho paralelo de GA 10 apresenta o horizonte pretendido por Steiner. A frase anterior descreve a vida anímica no pensamento expandindo-se ao ser espiritual. Estude o significado de um texto antes de trabalhar meditativamente com ele.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: In the pure streams of light
locator: Start Now! (2004), capture 115; verse presented among meditation material by Rudolf Steiner. English wording from the supplied edition; Portuguese is a new course translation.
edition: Start Now! (2004), capture 115; verse presented among meditation material by Rudolf Steiner. English wording from the supplied edition; Portuguese is a new course translation.
original:
In the pure streams of light
The world’s divinity shimmers.
In pure love for all beings
My soul’s divine nature rays out.

en.quote:
In the pure streams of light
The world’s divinity shimmers.
In pure love for all beings
My soul’s divine nature rays out.
en.note: The verse moves from light in the world to love radiating from the soul. Read those two directions, then hold the whole relation in attention; the exercise is more than repeating a comforting statement.

pt.quote:
Nas puras correntes de luz
Cintila a divindade do mundo.
No puro amor por todos os seres
Irradia a natureza divina de minha alma.
pt.note: O verso passa da luz no mundo ao amor que irradia da alma. Leia essas duas direções e mantenha a relação inteira na atenção; o exercício vai além de repetir uma frase reconfortante.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Parallel reading · How to Know Higher Worlds · Supporting qualities
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Das erste, was in dieser Beziehung der Geheimschüler beobachtet, ist die Regelung seines Gedankenlaufes (die sogenannte Gedankenkontrolle).

en.quote: The first thing the spiritual student attends to in this connection is the regulation of the course of thought, the so-called control of thought.
en.note: This parallel explanation in GA 10 connects thought practice with the development of spiritual capacities. The six qualities below complement one another: directed thought, initiative, equanimity, positivity, openness and their balance.

pt.quote: A primeira coisa a que o estudante espiritual atende nessa relação é a regulação do curso de seu pensar, o chamado controle do pensamento.
pt.note: Esta explicação paralela de GA 10 relaciona a prática do pensar ao desenvolvimento de capacidades espirituais. As seis qualidades abaixo se complementam: pensamento dirigido, iniciativa, equanimidade, positividade, abertura e equilíbrio.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Parallel reading · How to Know Higher Worlds · Self-observation
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Er soll seine Freuden, seine Leiden, seine Sorgen, seine Erfahrungen, seine Taten vor seiner Seele vorbeiziehen lassen.

en.quote: He should let his joys, his sufferings, his worries, his experiences and his deeds pass before his soul.
en.note: This related self-observation passage asks for distance from one’s earlier reactions. It does not itself specify reverse order. The backward review taught below adds the evening-to-morning sequence from the assigned meditation material; distinguish the direction of recall from the observing attitude.

pt.quote: Ele deve deixar passar diante de sua alma suas alegrias, seus sofrimentos, suas preocupações, suas experiências e suas ações.
pt.note: Este trecho relacionado pede distanciamento das reações anteriores. Ele não determina a ordem inversa. A retrospectiva abaixo acrescenta a sequência da noite para a manhã do material indicado; distinga direção da recordação e atitude observadora.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: Calendar of the Soul · Week 1 · Easter mood
locator: Weekly Meditations (2008), capture 11. Rudolf Steiner; English translation Christopher Bamford. New Portuguese course translation.
edition: Weekly Meditations (2008), capture 11. Rudolf Steiner; English translation Christopher Bamford. New Portuguese course translation.
original:
When the Sun speaks to human sense
From cosmic widths of space,
And from depths of soul
Joy unites with light in seeing—
Then, from sheaths of selfhood,
Thoughts move out to the ends of space,
Obscurely binding
Human essence to spirit’s being.

en.quote:
When the Sun speaks to human sense
From cosmic widths of space,
And from depths of soul
Joy unites with light in seeing—
Then, from sheaths of selfhood,
Thoughts move out to the ends of space,
Obscurely binding
Human essence to spirit’s being.
en.note: This verse joins an outward solar movement with inward joy and the movement of thought beyond its usual enclosure. Compare that movement with the other three complete verses below before selecting one for repeated study.

pt.quote:
Quando o Sol fala aos sentidos humanos
Das amplidões cósmicas do espaço,
E das profundezas da alma
A alegria se une à luz no ver—
Então, dos invólucros da individualidade,
Os pensamentos se movem até os confins do espaço,
Ligando obscuramente
A essência humana ao ser do espírito.
pt.note: Este verso une movimento solar exterior, alegria interior e pensamento que ultrapassa seu invólucro habitual. Compare esse movimento aos outros três versos completos abaixo antes de escolher um para estudo repetido.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: An Outline of Esoteric Science · GA 13 · The Rose Cross
edition: Original German text; new English and Brazilian Portuguese study translations.
original: Jedoch ist es gut, wenn man sich außer der Zeit, welche man der eigentlichen Versenkung widmet, öfters durch Gedanken und Gefühle der oben geschilderten Art den Aufbau des Bildes wiederholt, damit die Empfindung nicht verblasse.

en.quote: It is good, outside the time devoted to meditation itself, frequently to repeat the construction of the image through thoughts and feelings of the kind described above, so that the feeling does not fade.
en.note: This is Steiner’s distinction between preparing the Rose Cross and meditating with it. Preparation builds the meaning through plant, human passions and transformation; meditation holds the formed image with the feeling that preparation awakened.

pt.quote: É bom, fora do tempo dedicado à meditação propriamente dita, repetir frequentemente a construção da imagem pelos pensamentos e sentimentos descritos acima, para que o sentimento não enfraqueça.
pt.note: Steiner distingue preparar a Rosa-Cruz e meditar com ela. A preparação constrói o significado pela planta, pelas paixões humanas e pela transformação; a meditação mantém a imagem formada com o sentimento despertado.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: The Foundation Stone Meditation · first movement excerpt
locator: Opening of the first movement, lines 1–13
edition: Rudolf Steiner, GA 260, printed German version. The English and Portuguese below are new study translations made for this course, not the Adams, Wehrle or Bamford translations. Original line structure retained where practicable.
original:
Human soul!
You live in the limbs
That carry you through the world of space
Into the being of the spirit-ocean:
Practise spirit-remembering
In the depths of the soul,
Where, in the ruling
World-Creator-being,
Your own I
In the I of God
Comes into being;
And you will truly live
In human-world-being.

en.quote:
Human soul!
You live in the limbs
That carry you through the world of space
Into the being of the spirit-ocean:
Practise spirit-remembering
In the depths of the soul,
Where, in the ruling
World-Creator-being,
Your own I
In the I of God
Comes into being;
And you will truly live
In human-world-being.
en.note: The first movement connects limbs, space, spirit-remembering and the origin of the I. Read it as the first part of the complete meditation below; the later movements develop heart and lung, thinking, and the shared conclusion.

pt.quote:
Alma humana!
Tu vives nos membros
Que te levam pelo mundo do espaço
Ao ser do oceano espiritual:
Pratica a recordação do espírito
Nas profundezas da alma,
Onde, no regente
Ser Criador dos mundos,
O próprio Eu
No Eu de Deus
Vem a ser;
E viverás verdadeiramente
No ser humano-cósmico.
pt.note: O primeiro movimento relaciona membros, espaço, recordação do espírito e origem do Eu. Leia-o como primeira parte da meditação completa abaixo; os movimentos posteriores desenvolvem coração e pulmão, pensar e conclusão compartilhada.

author: Rudolf Steiner
title: In the pure streams of light
locator: Start Now! (2004), capture 115; verse presented among meditation material by Rudolf Steiner. English wording from the supplied edition; Portuguese is a new course translation.
edition: Start Now! (2004), capture 115; verse presented among meditation material by Rudolf Steiner. English wording from the supplied edition; Portuguese is a new course translation.

en.note: The ending returns self-knowledge to a relation with the world’s divinity. Use a complete, understood verse or Foundation Stone movement as your continuing focus, then review how your relation to its meaning develops over time.

pt.note: O final devolve o autoconhecimento à relação com a divindade do mundo. Use um verso completo e compreendido ou um movimento da Pedra Fundamental como foco contínuo e reveja como sua relação com o significado se desenvolve.
